text: How should militia be made too dear to spam?
context: Manpower upkeep can't do it for the North, which has more Manpower than it can use.

options.label: A. 0.5 Funds a turn for each column, and your 1.5 Manpower
options.rationale: No militia in the strongest army of any side. Costs the Republic 2.5 Funds a turn at the start.

options.label: B. 0.25 Funds a turn, and your 1.5 Manpower
options.rationale: Ends it for armies a side can keep; 28 columns can still be fed for a few turns from banked Manpower.

options.label: C. 4 Funds to raise
options.rationale: No new kind of upkeep. The bank can still feed a burst.

options.label: D. 3 Manpower a turn
options.rationale: Manpower only. The Republic could never keep more than 30 regiments.

text: Can militia attack without other troops?
context: Guns already can't. Militia beside a regiment, veterans, security forces, cavalry or tanks would still attack.

options.label: A. Yes, as today
options.rationale: Price and an attack of 2 already make it poor at attacking.

options.label: B. No, they need other troops with them
options.rationale: Forces mixed armies. Blocks the Republic's all-militia columns, and the computer player needs a change so it doesn't mistake militia for guns.

text: Should guns help hold ground too?
context: Today they add to the roll only when attacking.

options.label: A. Yes: +1 for every 3 defence points of guns, up to +2
options.rationale: Two full-strength guns give it all. Data only.

options.label: B. No, guns are for attacking

text: Should there be a bonus for mixing arms as such?
context: For example +1 for each kind beyond the first among foot, guns, armour, cavalry and air, up to +3. A new rule; you've asked me to prefer tuning.

options.label: A. No: the unit bonuses already do it
B. Yes, on attack
options.rationale: Simple to explain, and stacks on bonuses that are already large.

options.label: C. Yes, on attack and defence
options.rationale: Also gives defenders a reason to mix.

text: How many Factories can a city have?

options.label: A. One
options.rationale: Keeps today's incomes. 17 at the start, 8 more to build.

options.label: B. Up to three, and each Industry level today becomes one
options.rationale: More to build, but the Republic gains 5 Funds a turn at once.

context: Your note says the Factory enables artillery. Your chain answer says Barracks and Depot.

options.label: A. Barracks and Factory
options.rationale: Your note. Six places for the Republic and one for the North on turn 1.

options.label: B. Barracks and Depot
options.rationale: Three places each for the Republic and the North; first gun one turn sooner.

text: What do trucks, anti-air and aircraft need, now the old Factory is gone?

options.label: A. Trucks and anti-air a Depot; aircraft an Airfield
options.rationale: Short chains, and more places that can build each arm.

options.label: B. The merged Factory as well, as today

text: Knowing the odds, leave the South's opening alone?
context: You chose to leave it. A Republic that empties Madrid on turn 1 cuts the South's chance to 10% to 20% a turn.

options.label: A. Leave it
options.rationale: The gamble costs the Republic Madrid's garrison.

options.label: B. Give the South 3 more starting Manpower
options.rationale: It starves from turn 4 instead of turn 3.

text: Which end-turn sounds are worth keeping? Tick any.
context: If it's your own mix, paste its recipe in the notes. If none, one word for the sound you want helps most: drum, bell, bugle, cannon?

One deep church bell toll
Slow field drum: a short march figure, then two strikes
Kettledrum roll into one strike
Brass: two short chords and a long one
Pocket watch wound, then a tower clock strikes
Heavy ledger shut, then a rubber stamp
